claim_as_stated: Federal civilian workforce fell from ~2.31M (Sep 2024) to ~2.04M (Jan 2026); ~317k departures in 2025 (PPS / OPM data).
correct_statement: Federal civilian workforce fell from 2,313,216 (Sep 2024) to 2,035,344 (Jan 2026), a net drop of ~278k (12%) (Partnership for Public Service, from OPM data). The ~317,000 figure for 2025 departures is OPM Director Scott Kupor's own tally (X post, Dec 10, 2025: DRP ~144k, early retirement/buyouts ~21k, routine attrition ~129k, involuntary ~24k incl. RIF ~17k and probationary ~7k; ~68k hires by end-Aug), not a PPS figure. PPS counts 386,826 separations Jan 20, 2025-Jan 2026 (incl. 136,822 DRP, 10,436 RIF).
source_title: The Federal Workforce One Year into the Trump Administration (Fed Figures); Federal workforce down 317,000 (Bloomberg via Transport Topics)
source_publisher: Partnership for Public Service; Transport Topics/Bloomberg News reporting OPM Director
note: Do not attribute 317k to PPS and do not mix the two departure counts; they cover different periods and definitions. FEDmanager (Jan 2026) reports DRP as ~154k, so cite DRP component as approximate.

claim_as_stated: USFS and NPS each lost >25% of employees Sep 2024-Jan 2026; park rangers -34.1%; under-30 share of federal workforce 7.9%.
correct_statement: Per PPS analysis of OPM data, USFS and NPS each lost more than a quarter of employees Sep 2024-Jan 2026; park rangers fell 34.1%; under-30 share fell from 8.9% (Sep 2024) to 7.9% (Jan 2026).
source_title: The Federal Workforce One Year into the Trump Administration (Fed Figures)
note: PPS gives no exact USFS/NPS percentages. Other sources use different bases (e.g., FH-035 cites USDA OIG: USFS lost 16% in 2025); do not mix them.

claim_as_stated: EPA staff fell to ~12,849 (approx. -24%); median service of departing EPA staff ~30.3 years.
correct_statement: EPA had 12,849 employees at end of Jan 2026 (OPM data analyzed by Inside Climate News), a loss of more than 4,000 (24%) in the first year of the administration. The 30.3-year median service applies to the nearly 2,000 employees who left at year-end 2025 (vs 10.8 years for remaining staff), not to all 2025 departures.
source_title: EPA Hits 40-Year Lows in Staffing After Trump Targets Its Public Health Experts
note: Secondary analysis of OPM data (news). Scope the 30.3-year figure to year-end departures.

claim_as_stated: USFS hired no non-fire seasonal employees in 2025 and committed to ~2,000 for 2026.
correct_statement: Per a Mar 18, 2026 letter from Reps. Neguse and Huffman relaying agency information: with the exception of fire-related positions, USFS did not hire seasonal staff in 2025 due to budget constraints, and on Feb 12, 2026 committed to hiring 2,000 seasonals for 2026 (announced by Secretary Rollins).
source_title: Neguse, Huffman press US Forest Service for answers on staffing levels ahead of summer
note: No USDA/USFS primary press release located; announcement corroborated by press (WoodCentral 2026-02-16 citing Rollins/Schultz). Cite as congressional letter relaying agency statements.

claim_as_stated: AmeriCorps cuts of ~$400M hit conservation corps; FY2026 AmeriCorps status (settlement/stay to Feb 1, 2027).
correct_statement: In April 2025 AmeriCorps terminated nearly $400M in grants, hitting conservation corps. On Jun 5, 2025 Judge Boardman (D. Md.) preliminarily enjoined the cuts only in the 24 plaintiff states + DC; terminated programs there were reinstated and OMB released $184M+ in withheld funds (Aug 2025). A Sep 11, 2026 settlement with 23 AGs and two governors: AmeriCorps does not anticipate FY2026 mass grant terminations or member dismissals, must give 30 days notice of such actions, must commit substantially all FY2026 funds by Sep 30, 2026; litigation stayed through Feb 1, 2027.
source_title: Attorney General Ellison wins settlement blocking Trump Administration from dismantling AmeriCorps; Judge orders Trump administration to restore AmeriCorps as litigation continues
source_publisher: Minnesota Attorney General's Office; Maryland Matters
note: Stop presenting the $400M as a standing cut: it was largely reinstated in plaintiff jurisdictions; cuts persisted in non-plaintiff states. Settlement binds only to FY2026 and the coalition.

claim_as_stated: The U.S. Wildland Fire Service was established at DOI in January 2026, consolidating bureau fire programs (incl. BIA); ~5,780 federal + ~900 Tribal fire personnel.
correct_statement: SO 3448 (Jan 12, 2026) established the U.S. Wildland Fire Service at DOI (directed by SO 3443, Sep 10, 2025), unifying the fire programs of BIA, BLM, NPS and FWS plus the Office of Wildland Fire and Office of Aviation Services. DOI states USWFS employs 5,780 federal wildland fire personnel annually and supports ~900 Tribal wildland fire personnel.
source_title: About the U.S. Wildland Fire Service; SO 3448 - Establishment of the U.S. Wildland Fire Service
note: USFS fire was NOT moved; consolidation of USFS fire is only proposed in the FY2027 budget (TN-011). Tribal personnel are supported, not employed (ISDEAA programs).

claim_as_stated: USDA/USFS reorganization: HQ to Salt Lake City; nine regional offices closing; 57 of 77 research facilities closing; relocations through 2027.
correct_statement: Announced Mar 31-Apr 1, 2026: USFS HQ moves from Washington to Salt Lake City (~260 staff; ~130 remain in DC); all nine regional offices close in a shift to a state-based model with 15 state directors (facilities in R6 Portland, R8 Atlanta, R9 Milwaukee shut); 57 of 77 research facilities in 31 states close; relocations run from summer 2026 into 2027.
source_title: Forest Service to move HQ out of DC, shutter regional offices in sweeping overhaul; Forest Service will close research stations that study wildfire risk (AP)
source_publisher: Government Executive; AP via Hawaii Tribune-Herald
note: Press reports based on Chief Schultz email and internal memos; USDA news release referenced but not read. Implementation status after Jul 2026 not re-checked.

claim_as_stated: EO 14356 (Oct 15, 2025) created agency Strategic Hiring Committees approving every vacancy, with annual staffing plans.
correct_statement: EO 14356, Ensuring Continued Accountability in Federal Hiring (signed Oct 15, 2025), requires each agency to set up a Strategic Hiring Committee (deputy head, chief of staff, others) within 30 days that approves the creation or filling of each vacancy, and annual staffing plans (first within 60 days, then each fiscal year) coordinated with OPM and OMB, with quarterly updates from FY2026 Q2. Exceptions include immigration enforcement, national security and public safety. No sunset.
source_title: Executive Order 14356: Ensuring Continued Accountability in Federal Hiring
note: The EO sets no hiring ratio; the 1-for-4 ratio applies via OPM/OMB guidance (Nov 5, 2025) until plans are submitted. OPM issued further Guidance on Annual Staffing Plans on Jul 30, 2026.

claim_as_stated: OPM Merit Hiring Plan (May 29, 2025); self-assessment questionnaires may not rank candidates after Sep 30, 2025; technical-assessment adoption rates (91% self-report-only in FY2025; 34.3% technical by FY2026 Q2).
correct_statement: OPM issued the Merit Hiring Plan May 29, 2025. From Sep 30, 2025 agencies may use self-assessment questionnaires only for minimum qualifications/eligibility, not rating and ranking (exceptions: seasonal, GS-04 and below, OPM-authorized). In FY2025, 91.23% (41,386) of delegated examining (DE) announcements relied solely on self-report questionnaires; in FY2026 Q2, 34.3% of DE announcements used technical and/or off-the-shelf assessments.
source_title: Chance to Compete Act of 2024 Consolidated Report to Congress; CTCA Governmentwide Implementation Plan for Transition to Technical Assessments
note: Both percentages are for delegated examining announcements only, not all hiring. Essay Q3 stayed in AFGE v. Kupor (Sep 2026; FH-032).

claim_as_stated: OPM Phase One occupational series consolidation memo (Apr 24, 2026): 115 series; 0410/0437/0480/0487->0401; 0455->0404; 0029->0303; 0688->0601.
correct_statement: OPM CHCO memo Modernization and Consolidation of Occupational Series (Apr 24, 2026; V. Hinton) issued a PROPOSED Phase One list of 115 series (~4,926 employees) for realignment, incl. 0410/0437/0480/0487->0401, 0455->0404, 0029->0303, 0688->0601 (also 0023->0186, 0190->0101, 0459->4701, 0698->0640, 0965->0901, 1372/1380->1301, 1374->1311). Agency feedback due May 11, 2026; OPM to finalize decisions after review. No final-decision memo appears on the CHCO published-memos index as of Oct 23, 2026.
source_title: Modernization and Consolidation of Occupational Series (CHCO memo)
note: Say "proposed for realignment", not "consolidated". Final status not confirmed; agencies could request retention.

claim_as_stated: OPM issued competency-based classification and qualification standards for 2210 on Apr 13, 2026 under the Federal Workforce Competency Initiative (FWCI); targets of 300+ / 600+ series.
correct_statement: On Apr 13, 2026 OPM issued four CHCO memos: competency-based position classification standard and qualification standard for 2210, job aids, and FWCI General and Technical Competencies and Competency Frameworks (FWCI survey memo followed Apr 27). OPM's Dec 2025 CTCA report targets updating 300+ GS series by end of FY2026 and an additional 300+ (600+ total) by end of FY2027.
source_title: CHCO Council Published Memos index; Chance to Compete Act of 2024 Consolidated Report to Congress
note: As of Oct 23, 2026 the CHCO index lists competency-based standards only for 2210; the FY2026 300+ target appears not met via published memos (memo index only; not proof).

claim_as_stated: Schedule Policy/Career final rule (Feb 6, 2026; effective Mar 9, 2026) and a June 2026 EO moving ~8,000 employees.
correct_statement: OPM final rule Improving Performance, Accountability and Responsiveness in the Civil Service (RIN 3206-AO80; 91 FR 5580) published Feb 6, 2026, effective Mar 9, 2026. EO 14410, Implementing Schedule Policy/Career in the Excepted Service, signed Jun 3, 2026 (published Jun 10, 2026), placed positions listed in its appendix into Schedule Policy/Career; press and Lawfare analysis put this at ~8,000 employees in ~4,800 positions across 54 agencies (97% GS-15 or above).
source_title: Improving Performance, Accountability and Responsiveness in the Civil Service (final rule); Executive Order 14410
source_publisher: OPM (Federal Register); Daily Compilation of Presidential Documents
note: The ~8,000 figure is not in the EO text (appendix); cite MeriTalk/Lawfare for it. Litigation pending (PEER, AFGE, NTEU, GAP).

claim_as_stated: OPM memo of Aug 27, 2026 on AI use in hiring (AI-drafted PDs generally not high-impact when humans adopt them).
correct_statement: OPM memo Use of Artificial Intelligence in the Federal Hiring Process (Aug 27, 2026; Director Kupor) treats drafting job-opportunity artifacts incl. position descriptions as generally not high-impact under M-25-21 when drafting does not affect access to employment and the responsible official independently reviews, revises and adopts the draft; adoption without substantive documented review is high-impact. Rating/ranking/scoring is presumed high-impact. 5 CFR 300.103 job analysis applies; applicant data only in agency-authorized tools.
source_title: Use of Artificial Intelligence in the Federal Hiring Process (CHCO memo)
note: Memo states these are OPM views developed with OMB, not official OMB determinations; agencies make their own M-25-21 determinations.

claim_as_stated: Conservation job postings fell 29.4% YoY (Mar-Sep 2025); paid internships -43.8%; AmeriCorps postings -42%.
correct_statement: Postings on the Conservation Job Board fell 29.4% year over year for Mar 1-Sep 30, 2025; paid internships fell 43.8% and AmeriCorps positions 42% (with a survey of 337 conservation employers).
source_title: Analysis Of Conservation Job Postings Shows Significant Decrease During 2025
note: Scope is one job board, not the whole conservation labor market; analyst not named in the article.

claim_as_stated: FY2026 Interior-Environment appropriations approx. $42.56bn (-1.9% YoY), well above the President's request.
correct_statement: FY2026 Interior-Environment appropriations enacted in P.L. 119-74, Division C (Jan 23, 2026) total $42.56bn, down $809M (1.9%) from FY2025 ($43.37bn), vs a President's request of $26.85bn. Total includes $2.85bn wildfire suppression cap adjustment and $5.31bn IHS FY2027 advance appropriations. USFS $8.61bn (request $2.31bn); NPS $3.27bn; EPA $8.82bn.
source_title: Interior, Environment, and Related Agencies: Overview of FY2026 Appropriations (R48726)

correct_statement: OPM launched the Federal Workforce Data (FWD) site at data.opm.gov in Jan 2026, replacing FedScope, with monthly data updates.
source_title: OPM Launches New Workforce Data Site; New federal workforce data site goes live with more current information
source_publisher: U.S. Office of Personnel Management; FEDweek
note: Release lists retirement eligibility, telework, admin leave, performance ratings and hiring activity; series-level content not described in the release.

claim_as_stated: Natural Resources Management named a Tier 2 occupational group for Chance to Compete technical assessments, full implementation FY2028.
correct_statement: OPM's July 2026 CTCA implementation plan places Natural Resources Management in Tier 2 (Medium Priority, with Transportation and Physical Sciences), addressed after Tier 1 (IT, Accounting and Budget, Legal) matures. No Tier 2 completion date is given; FY2028 is the governmentwide full-implementation target tied to the final (Tier 3) phase.
source_title: Chance to Compete Act of 2024 Governmentwide Implementation Plan for Transition to Technical Assessments (Report to Congress)
note: Report is internally inconsistent (transition "by the end of 2027" vs full implementation end of FY2028). Do not say NRM will be fully implemented by FY2028 specifically.
